get.description: Each key carries its owner's username. Never the key or its hash. Lists the caller's own keys and those of owners whose roles the caller dominates; the rest are left out before the page is cut, so the total does not count them. A key whose owner no longer exists needs core:admin.

get.summary: Read one API key by ID
get.description: The owner's, or a manager's who dominates the owner. Any other caller gets the answer a missing key gets.

patch.summary: Disable, re-enable or revoke any key by ID
patch.description: Re-enabling needs an interactive sign-in; another user's key needs an interactiveOnly() manager who dominates the owner.

get.summary: Query the audit log, newest first
get.description: Filters: since and until (RFC 3339), actor (a user id), action (a prefix such as core.auth.), outcome (success, failure, denied, error) and target (module, module/kind or module/kind/id). The cursor continues a query with the same filters. A record whose action is about an identity or a credential (core.auth.*, core.user.*, core.apikey.*, core.session.*, core.invite.*, core.templogin.*, core.identity.*, core.bootstrap.*, core.permission.deny and the like), and a record whose action core does not classify (a module's own), is left out unless the caller holds core:users.manage, who also alone sees actor.credential_id and actor.client_addr. A caller without core:users.manage has withheld records read and dropped by the query, at most 10,000 per request: a page may then be short or empty with a next_cursor, and the client follows cursors until there is none. The auth-disabled principal is refused with 403 interactive_required.

get.summary: Export the audit log as NDJSON
get.description: The same filters as the query, without a cursor or limit; one JSON record per line, newest first, each as the query returns it. The export is recorded (core.audit.export) before the first line and does not start if that record cannot be written. A read that fails part-way ends the stream with the line {"error":"export_incomplete"}.

post.summary: Exchange the bootstrap token for an administrator API key
post.description: The key and a generated password (when the account is created) are shown once. A wrong, expired or spent token is the same 401 bootstrap_invalid.

post.summary: Accept an invite: create the account and open a session
post.description: Sets the session cookie. The invite is re-checked at this moment: its creator must still exist and still be able to assign its role.

post.summary: Show what an invite token would create
post.description: The token travels in the body. An unknown, spent or expired token is the same 401 link_invalid.

post.summary: Sign in with a username and password
post.description: Sets the session cookie; the body carries no token. An unknown name, a wrong password and an account without a password are the same 401 invalid_credentials.

post.summary: End the current session and clear its cookie

get.summary: Finish a sign-in at the provider's redirect
get.description: Opens a web session, or on the native-app branch mints the app's code before any session exists and redirects to the app.

get.summary: Send the browser to an identity provider
get.description: redirect_uri (alias callback) with code_challenge selects the native-app branch: an unlisted redirect_uri is an inline 400 with no Location, a method other than S256 is a 400.
Ids and kinds only: never a client id or a secret.

post.summary: Create the first administrator
post.description: Open only while no user exists, and then only with the bootstrap token or from a local request (05-authn §4.6). Once setup is closed (a user exists, or the caller may not use it) the answer is 403 setup_closed whatever the body says, so a closed setup reveals nothing. While it is open, a wrong, expired or spent bootstrap token is 401 bootstrap_invalid.

get.summary: Whether the app has users and whether authentication is on

post.summary: Spend a temp-login or reset link and open a session
post.description: Sets the session cookie. A reset link needs new_password, a plain link refuses it.

get.description: The one realtime stream. topic is repeatable and is an exact topic name, a module wildcard (module.*) or * (the default); exclude removes topics with the same grammar; key narrows to one entity; last_event_id (or the Last-Event-ID header, which wins) resumes after an event id inside the server's bounded window. An exact topic you may not see is 403 topic_not_permitted and an unknown one is 400 unknown_topic; a wildcard silently leaves out topics you may not see. Over the stream limits the answer is 429 (per user and credential class) or 503, with Retry-After. Every refusal is a problem+json status before the stream starts. The stream carries unnamed frames: id: <bootNonce>-<seq> and data: {topic, ts, key, data}, a comment line per heartbeat, and the id-less control frames core.stream.opened.v1, core.stream.reset.v1 (restart, gap or overflow: refetch over REST) and core.stream.closed.v1 (shutdown, credential_revoked or permission_revoked: reconnect). Each event is filtered for you at send time, replays included.

Every declared topic, by name: the permission that observes it, its payload JSON Schema, whether it is durable (an outbox topic, with its partitions) and its notification and realtime metadata. The catalog is the same for every caller of the route.

get.summary: The signed-in user, its scopes and how it signed in

patch.description: An e-mail change is an identity change: it clears the verified mark and revokes what the old address granted.

get.description: Never the key itself or its hash.

post.summary: Mint an API key for the caller
post.description: The key is shown once. Every scope must be held by the caller now; a key mints only for itself and only within its own expiry (05-authn §4.4).

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's keys

patch.summary: Disable, re-enable or revoke one of the caller's keys
patch.description: A key manages only keys it may create; re-enabling needs an interactive sign-in, disabling and revoking do not (a restriction widens nothing).

put.description: Self only: {current, new}. There is no target-user field; an admin sends a reset link instead. Every other session of the account ends.

get.description: Public IDs only, never a token.

delete.summary: End one of the caller's sessions

get.summary: The server manifest: core and app identity, the enabled modules and what UI each may contribute
get.description: The shell intersects this list with its compile-time registry and drops what is not declared (07 §7.5). A disabled module is absent from modules; disabled_modules lists them for a caller holding core:admin and is absent for every other caller.

get.summary: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of one owner, as <owner>.json
get.description: Takes <owner>.json, the owner being core or a module ID. A caller who is not signed in gets 401 unless core.http.openapi.public is true; an unknown owner is 404. The body is the document the build produced, byte for byte.

Every declared consumer, enabled or not, with its lag, pending, retrying and dead counts and its topic's intake backlog. A disabled module's consumer is listed with the backlog the store keeps for it (retained_backlog). A count marked capped is a floor: the store counts at most 1000 per partition. What the relay will not work on until an operator acts (a topic, a pair, a family of stored keys) is listed under stopped, beside the page and whole on every page, each with a closed cause token.

delete.description: Advances every cursor of the consumer to the head of its topic and clears its retries, discarding the messages it has not taken over; answers how many it skipped. Dead letters stay, and messages sequenced after the purge are delivered normally. It is the only way a disabled module's retained messages are discarded. Needs an interactive sign-in (not an API key). Audited as core.outbox.backlog_purge before the purge runs: when the record cannot be written the answer is 503 and nothing was purged; the purge then records how many messages it skipped, or the failure it ended in. The purge runs to its end even if the client hangs up. 404 when the consumer is unknown or has no backlog (it never ran); 409 when the topic is not available to this build or its partition count changed.

get.description: Dead letters in (consumer, topic, seq) order, at most 500 per page; follow next_cursor until there is none (a page that ends exactly at the last letter still carries one, and the next page is empty). A letter shows its consumer, topic, seq, partition, attempts, the token that says why it died, and its idempotency key; never its payload or its key. A dead letter stays until an operator retries or discards it.

delete.description: Deletes the dead letter for good. Audited as core.outbox.dead_discard before the delete runs: when the record cannot be written the answer is 503 and nothing was discarded; a discard that then fails is recorded as the failure it was. 404 and 409 as for a retry.

post.summary: Retry one dead letter
post.description: Hands the message back to its consumer alone, at the end of the stream under a new seq, and deletes the dead letter. Audited as core.outbox.dead_retry before the retry runs: when the record cannot be written the answer is 503 and nothing was retried; a retry that then fails is recorded as the failure it was. 404 when the consumer is unknown or has no dead letter at seq; 409 when the letter changed under the operation (list it again).

get.summary: List the roles, seed and custom, with their permissions and pending seed additions
get.description: Newest release additions waiting for an administrator are in pending_seed (05-rbac §4.8). A stored role that cannot be decoded is left out and logged.

post.summary: Create a custom role
post.description: name is custom.<slug>. The caller must hold every permission it names (a wildcard needs the pattern itself or core:admin): 403 scope_escalation otherwise. A name in use is 409 role_exists.

delete.description: Needs If-Match: the role's version. A role any user holds is 409 role_in_use: ?reassign= is not built, so take the role from its holders first. admin is 409 role_locked and a seed role 409 seed_role_locked.

get.description: version is what a write names in If-Match.

patch.summary: Change a custom role's title, description or permissions
patch.description: Needs If-Match: the role's version (428 without it, 412 when it is stale). A field the body omits keeps its value; permissions replaces the set. The caller must hold every permission of the old and the new set (403 scope_escalation). admin is 409 role_locked and a seed role 409 seed_role_locked. A change that takes core:admin from the last role that grants it to an active user is 409 last_admin.

post.summary: Make a seed role's pending release additions effective
post.description: The one write a seed role allows (05-rbac §4.8). Needs If-Match: the role's version. The caller must hold every permission of the resulting set (403 scope_escalation). A role with nothing pending is 409 no_pending_seed.

get.summary: Every key of the sections the caller may read, as {path: key state}
get.description: A secret key shows only whether a value is set, its source and who wrote it; never a value, a mask or a hash.

patch.summary: Store and unset settings in one commit
patch.description: Body {set: {path: value}, unset: [path]}. 400 unknown_key; 403 permission_denied (need: key to the section's write permission) or protection_required (need: key to the protection level); 409 locked (locked_by: key to the operator layer); 422 validation_failed (one error per key); 500 on a storage failure. 200 carries restart_pending and post_commit_error when present. A secret key's value is a JSON string and is never returned.

get.summary: The settings schema (JSON Schema 2020-12), one property per section the caller may read
get.description: Vendor keywords: x-mediacore-reload, x-mediacore-protect, x-mediacore-secret, x-mediacore-fail-closed; secret keys carry writeOnly.

post.summary: Stage a factory reset; it runs when the service restarts
post.description: Body {kind: "factory" (default) or "store", confirm: "RESET", delete_library_files?: bool (default false), library_root?, library_file_count?}. 422 confirm_required without the confirm; 422 library_files_confirm_required, carrying the current library_root and library_file_count, when delete_library_files is true and they do not match the preflight; 422 reset_request_invalid; 400 reset_refused; 409 swap_pending. Nothing is staged on any refusal. 200 {reset_id, message} plus library_root and library_file_count when files will be deleted. Files deleted by a reset are not restored.

post.summary: Receive a browser's Content-Security-Policy violation report
post.description: Accepts application/csp-report (report-uri), application/reports+json (Reporting API, an array) and application/json, at most ten reports per request. Public because a browser sends a report with no credential. Only the violated directive is read, matched against the CSP directive names (anything else is counted as other); no URL or blocked-uri is logged or kept. Answers 204 for any well-formed request, whether or not it held a report.

post.summary: Report one UI diagnostic
post.description: The shell reports each diagnostic kind once per page load (07 §7.5.2). Only kind and module are read, and both are matched against closed lists: an unknown kind or module is counted as other, and no submitted text is logged or kept. Answers 204 whether or not the server accepts diagnostics.

get.description: Filter by status or role.
Never a token or a link.

post.summary: Invite a user
post.description: The role must be one the caller may assign. The link is shown once.

post.summary: Mint an API key for another user
post.description: Needs dominance over the user and scopes the user's roles hold too. The key is shown once.

post.summary: Disable a user
Enable a user
Mint a password reset link for a user
post.description: There is no route that sets another user's password. The link is shown once and ends every session of the user.

post.summary: Acknowledge one core:admin holder a restore listed for review
post.description: After a restore with no pre-swap store every core:admin holder is listed for review, and health reports restore_admins_review until an interactive core:admin session has acknowledged each one (05-rbac 7.1); this route acknowledges the holder in the path and audits core.role.review_admin. The holder is looked up in the restore report, not among the users: an account that is not listed (never listed, already acknowledged, or deleted and acknowledged since) is 404 not_found, so acknowledging twice answers 404 the second time and records nothing. Acknowledging yourself is allowed.

delete.summary: End one of a user's sessions

post.summary: Mint a temp-login link for a user
